method_card.title: Solving Quadratic Inequalities
method_card.content:
A quadratic inequality asks for which values of \(x\) a quadratic is above or below zero. Solve the matching equation for the roots, sketch the parabola, then read off the region.

Below zero (\(< 0\), \(\leq 0\)) sits between the roots; above zero (\(> 0\), \(\geq 0\)) sits outside them. Use a closed bound for \(\leq\) or \(\geq\), an open bound for \(<\) or \(>\).
method_card.example:
Solve \(x^2 - 3x - 4 > 0\).

\((x-4)(x+1) = 0\) gives roots \(-1\) and \(4\). The U-shape is above zero outside the roots, so \(x < -1\) or \(x > 4\).

steps: When \(x^2\) has a coefficient, split the middle term to factorise; roots may be fractions.
Pick the region as usual (between for \(< 0\), outside for \(> 0\)), then read off the value asked for.
For a repeated root or a discriminant question, think about whether the curve touches or clears the axis.
